reasons.agent: The two Hub tasks change flow staffing and a payload other parts rely on. That is Tier 2 work, so Opus builds them.
reasons.builders: DeveloperOpus for the Hub tasks; Developer (Sonnet) for the small F1083 refusal and the UI pre-fill, to save quota; QA2 for the two drive tasks. QA2 is named as a checker nowhere, so today's flow does not withhold it from fresh work.
reasons.cron: Every five minutes, the default; a task waiting on a check is picked up within that.
reasons.level: Reviewed: someone other than the builder approves, and missing evidence is reported rather than blocking.
reasons.mode: Six tasks in a clear order: write-drive first, then one-driver and plan-in-spec in parallel; a flow runs them as their prerequisites clear.
reasons.reviewer: QA checks every task, and its review also tests the running product. It builds none of them, so it never checks its own work.
reasons.stop: Stop when the six tasks are done. Restart :8000 only after that (see the hazard in the design).
reasons.tester: No separate tester: QA, the checker, tests as part of its review (one checker per task, operator 2026-10-29).

design:
Decided with the operator on 2026-10-29:
- **One checker per task.** The checker both drives the product and gives the verdict. New documents are no longer offered separate reviewer and tester roles. In an old document that names both a reviewer and a tester, the tester becomes the checker, because the checker is the one who drives the product.
- **Checks follow the level.** At Fast the builder or the lead approves and no check is handed out (`builds.py:5`, `fast_approval_refusal`); at Reviewed and Gated the check goes to the checker.
- **The spec carries the plan.** The recommendation the author wrote stays as written. Starting a build adds the operator's choices to the document beside it, labelled as the operator's. Agents read both and can tell them apart. The document holds the running build and the most recent ended one; older builds stay on the build record only, so the tracked file does not grow with every restart.
- **A named person who is gone holds the work.** A task whose builder or checker is not an open agent is held, saying so on the task, rather than handed to someone else: the plan named a person, and quietly substituting another hides that the plan is broken.
- **By hand means the operator starts the work.** A hand build only places tasks on the board under their builders. A task stays in Pending with its builder named, because a move to Assigned starts that agent automatically today (`assigned_task_start`). The operator also sends each check by hand.
- **The driver that started a build is the only one.** Nothing else attaches a flow or loop while the build runs. The refusal lives on the job-creation route (`POST /jobs`, `api/v1/jobs.py:839`), which `create_flow` and `create_loop` call; the build's own flow must still be creatable.

**Hazard (Tier 2).** `people-get-their-tasks` changes how a flow staffs work (`scheduler.py`). The operator's `:8000` Hub runs this checkout, so once that task merges to master the new staffing takes effect at that Hub's next restart, including for any flow it is then running. Restart `:8000` only after the flow building this slice has finished. Rollback: revert the merge and restart; the document payload change is additive (old reviewer/tester names keep building), so no data migration is needed.

open_questions.question: When an old document names both a reviewer and a tester, which becomes the checker? Answer: the tester (operator, 2026-10-29).
In a hand build, does a task with a builder sit in Pending or Assigned? Answer: Pending with the builder named (operator accepted, 2026-10-29).
A task whose builder is not an open agent: hold it or give it to the builders list? Answer: hold it and say so (operator, 2026-10-29).
How many builds does the document keep? Answer: the running build and the most recent ended one (operator, 2026-10-29).
Who sends the check in a hand build? Answer: the operator, by hand (operator, 2026-10-29).

problem:
Today a spec names the people who build and check it in seven overlapping places: `delivery.agent`, `builders`, `reviewer`, `reviewers`, `tester`, `tasks[].builder` and `tasks[].reviewer`. The Build dialog pre-selects only two of them. It shows `delivery.reviewer` as a line of text, and never shows `tester` or a task's own reviewer. So the agent the spec chose to check the work is not pre-selected (operator, 2026-10-29).

The operator's choices at Build are kept only on the build record. An agent told to build reads the recommendation as though it were the decision. On 2026-10-29 Architect started a flow on a document the operator was building by hand, and the Hub accepted it (F1083).

At Build, a task's builder becomes its assignee (`builds.cover_tasks`, `builds.py:244`). But a flow draws fresh work only from the build-wide `builders` list (`scheduler.py:1836`), and it withholds fresh work from any agent the document names to judge work (`_agents_withheld_from_fresh_work`, F767). So a task given to an agent outside that list, or to an agent who also checks, may never be worked, and no test covers this. The only test of per-task builders covers a hand build (`test_a_declared_builder_is_assigned_when_the_build_starts`).

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: one person checks it. Having two roles that each judge the work is what left the dialog with fields nobody filled.
requirements.statement: A change document names, for each task, at most one builder and at most one checker, plus a build-wide default builder and default checker; the checker of a task is the single agent who both tests it and records its verdict.

requirements.rationale: Approved documents are not reopened just to rename a field, and a build of one must not lose its reviewer. The tester wins because the single checker drives the product (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: A document saved before this change that names `reviewer`, `tester` or a task's own `reviewer` builds with those agents as its checkers, without the document being edited. A task's own reviewer is that task's checker; otherwise the tester, if named, is the default checker, else the reviewer.

The Build dialog opens with every person the document names already selected: the default builder, the default checker, and each task's builder and checker. No person the document names is shown only as text, or left out.

Starting a build writes the operator's choices into the spec document: the driver, the level, the default builder and checker, each task's builder and checker, the lead, the budget cap, the window and the landing. They sit beside the author's recommendation, labelled as the operator's, and the recommendation is left unchanged.

`read_spec_document` returns the document's running build, with every choice listed in choices-in-the-spec, marked as the operator's choice and kept apart from `delivery`. A turn started to work on or check one of the build's tasks names the build's driver and that task's builder and checker.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: the last ended build explains the latest change of plan; a full history would grow the tracked file on every restart.
requirements.statement: When a build stops or finishes, the spec document shows that build as ended, stopped or finished, with when, and `read_spec_document` no longer reports it as running. The document holds at most the running build and the most recent ended build; an older ended build leaves the document and stays on the build record.

requirements.rationale: F1083: a second driver re-pointed a hand build's tasks at a flow the operator never chose.
requirements.statement: Creating a flow or a loop for a document whose build is running is refused with 409, and the refusal names the build and its driver. No task's flow or loop changes as a result. Starting a build that is driven by a flow still creates that flow.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: hold rather than hand to someone else, so a broken plan shows instead of being quietly substituted.
requirements.statement: In a flow-driven build, a task whose builder is an open agent is worked only by that agent, whether or not the agent is in the build-wide builders list or is named as a checker elsewhere. While that builder is busy, the task waits for them and is not given to anyone else. A task whose builder is not an open agent is held, given to nobody, and says on the task that its builder is not an open agent.

In a flow- or lead-driven build at Reviewed or Gated, a finished task's check goes to that task's checker, or to the default checker when the task names none, and never to the agent that built it. A checker that is not an open agent holds the check and says so on the task, rather than passing the check to someone else. At Fast no check is handed out.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: by hand is for me to start it, and I send the check myself. Pending rather than Assigned, because a move to Assigned starts the agent today.
requirements.statement: In a hand-driven build, every task whose builder is an open agent shows on the board in Pending with that agent named as its builder, and its checker named. No run is started and no message or queued input reaches any agent until the operator asks one to pick up a task or a check.
In a lead-driven build, the lead's brief names each task's builder and checker, and a task the lead hands to anyone other than its named builder is recorded with who it went to.

in_scope: One builder and one checker per task, plus a build-wide default builder and default checker
Existing documents that name a reviewer and/or tester still build
The Build dialog pre-selects every person the document names (data only; the redesign is slice build-dialog-overhaul)
The operator's build choices written into the spec document and readable by agents
Refusing a second driver on a document whose build is running
Each driver (flow, lead, hand) gives each task to its builder and its check to its checker
A task whose named builder or checker is not an open agent is held and says so
non_goals: Recommending who builds and checks each task (slice recommended-people)
Redesigning the Build dialog's layout or style (slice build-dialog-overhaul)
Board filters or readable task ids (slices board-by-spec, readable-task-ids)
Changing what the levels Fast, Reviewed and Gated decide
Changing a running build's people after it starts; to change them, the build is stopped and started again
Starting agents automatically in a hand build, or sending a hand build's checks automatically
Keeping more than the running and the most recent ended build in the document
